newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP Leykam agrees Dutch restructuring.
newsitem.headline: KNP Leykam agrees Dutch restructuring.

text.p: Dutch paper group KNP BT said on Thursday it had reached agreement with unions on the restructuring of the Dutch operations of its paper-making arm KNP Leykam.
"The social plan (reached) will apply to the paper factories in Maastricht and Nijmegen as well as to the service organisation KNP Leykam Services," KNP said in a news release.

KNP BT said in January it intended to cut 1,000 of the 4,600 jobs at KNP Leykam, leading to a cost saving of 100 million guilders per year. Some 350 of the job cuts would be in the Netherlands, 500 in Austria and 110 in Belgium.
KNP BT is in the middle of a 1.2 billion guilder investment programme in Leykam to boost production and productivity.
In 1996, Leykam posted a net loss of 496 million Austrian schillings, against a profit of 2.16 billion schillings in 1995.
KNP Leykam is 69.5 percent owned by KNP BT and 30.5 percent by Austria's Leykam-Muerztaler. KNP BT owns a 72.3 percent stake in Leykam-Muerztaler.
